beur-hagra/3:_: Seif 3: And there are those who say, etc. So too in Orach Mishpat, and as written in Yerushalmi they instituted that a minor reads the Megillah, etc. This is according to R' Yehuda in Megillah 19b, as the Gemara there speaks of a minor in such a case; see Tosafot there d.h. v'Rabbi Yehuda, etc. It appears his reason for ruling like R' Yehuda is from Tosafot's difficulty there, and he holds the sugya in Berachot chapter 3 that a son blesses for his father, and the sugya in Pesachim that R' Shimon and R' Yehuda said aggadah — all follow R' Yehuda; and that he does not discharge with Hallel — he holds like the Geonim that Hallel is d'oraisa; but Tosafot there answer it speaks where the minor ate enough to be satiated, which is also one of the rabbinic matters; so too Mordechai there; and so the second answer in Berachot 15a d.h. v'Rabbi Yehuda; and another answer there that in the evening prayer it is different — see there; and from Pesachim they answer a blind person is different since he was already obligated; and as Ran wrote in Kiddushin end of chapter 1 in the name of aggadah they were not blind from birth; but in Tosafot Rosh HaShanah 34a d.h. ha, etc., not so — it implies he holds like the Orach Mishpat mentioned who wrote there; however one may reject that a minor can discharge an obligated rabbinic person like a son blessing for his father, and he counts toward seven and discharges others — 18 in Megillah for R' Yehuda, etc. — see there he wrote therefore they said aggadah; and therefore R' Yehuda says in chapter 3 of Megillah whoever did not see lights, etc. — it implies if he saw he discharges even though exempt from all mitzvot; rather according to what Tosafot wrote in Megillah that a blind person is different since he was already obligated, apparently there was no difficulty from Megillah; but it is not so — it implies from R' Yehuda's words that he may not recite because he never benefited, and the Gemara challenges the Rabbanan from this — why? — and answers because of R' Yehuda; it implies in other rabbinic matters he agrees one can discharge even if he never saw; therefore it must be as Tosafot wrote in Rosh HaShanah there. However for a blind person there is no practical difference, for we hold not like R' Yehuda — anonymous Mishnah in chapter HaChovel is not like him, as written; and likewise the Pesachim sugya is not like him, as written, that a blind person is exempt only from saying the Hagadah — they deduced there: who said aggadah in Beit R' Yehuda? — they did not deduce on Kiddush and all year; furthermore they concluded there that even in Hagadah they are obligated; so Mordechai in chapter 2 of Megillah — see there; the difference is only for a minor.
biur-halacha/3:ב: And for us, where each one, etc. — see Mishna Berurah; see below siman 677 in Magen Avraham s.k. 8 who brought Maharash Galante who holds that even for us, where each kindles a light, minors are exempt [for although obligated in chinuch, that is in a matter where the adult is obligated by law; but here for an adult too there is only one because of hidur mitzvah, the minor is not obligated in chinuch for it]. I later found in Meiri who also wrote thus: "Those who are mehaderin in the mitzvah — a light for each one in proportion to the number of adult household members" — end. What Machatzit HaShekel wrote there to reconcile Maharash Galante with the Rama is a great strain. In truth what Magen Avraham brought there — this is because the Mechaber wrote at first that per the Mechaber's view it speaks where he has a separate household, therefore he concludes "and it is possible even for us, etc.," and he is only obligated when he has a separate household.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1: Kindling accomplishes the mitzvah and not placement, etc.; therefore a lamp that was burning all day, etc. NB: The Rambam's wording here: a lamp that was burning all day — to say one extinguishes, blesses, and kindles, for kindling is the mitzvah and not placement — end. I saw in Peri Chadash who questioned him: from his wording it implies if placement accomplished the mitzvah there would be no need for extinguishing, and this contradicts the Gemara that challenges there — if you would think placement accomplishes the mitzvah, why extinguish, raise, kindle, and place? If so, even for the view that placement accomplishes the mitzvah, extinguishing is required. What Peri Chadash answered with two answers does not appear correct. The second answer — the Rambam speaks of kindling for Hanukkah — according to Tosafot there this certainly does not appear correct, for then he should have explained, especially since the Gemara challenges from extinguishing and raising — it implies he holds that anonymously "a lamp burning all day" does not speak of Hanukkah; if so, since anonymously it implies Shabbat lights, the Rambam should have explained; also why abandon the explicit Gemara law speaking of Shabbat and cite another law not explicit in the Gemara? The first answer Peri Chadash wrote — his intent and for precision: placement is not required; if placement accomplished the mitzvah, placement would also be required — this too does not appear correct, for the Rambam should have explained and not relied on precision. However it appears there is no difficulty: Tosafot there truly questioned: if placement accomplishes the mitzvah, why extinguish? — it is no worse than kindling accidentally; in my humble opinion it fits well. One may say this is similar to slaughter: we hold intention is not required for slaughter, and even if the knife fell without intent it is valid; however if it fell by itself it is invalid, for an act is in any case required; if slaughtered accidentally it is valid — it proves accidental act counts as act, only intention they lack; but they have act, and it is preferable to falling by itself. So too in Hanukkah: even for the view placement accomplishes the mitzvah — that is only that kindling l'shem mitzvah is not required, and accidental kindling helps, for even though they lack intention, and even for those who hold mitzvot require intention, they agree in rabbinic matters intention is not required — only if fit for intention; since fit for mixing, mixing does not block; since accidental they lack intention, their kindling does not help if kindling accomplishes the mitzvah; also since they are not obligated, they cannot discharge others; nevertheless if placement accomplishes the mitzvah, accidental kindling helps. However if it kindled by itself it certainly does not help, for in any case human act is required in kindling, and kindled by itself does not help; therefore likewise if it burned from erev Shabbat, since the first act is gone, as we say in Berachot regarding kindling from my brands the first pillar is gone; and likewise water turning a wheel and slaughtering — the first force is gone and afterward it is by itself; so too here the first force is gone and afterward it is as kindled by itself; therefore it is worse than accidental kindling, for in any case act is required, and this is by itself. Tosafot's question is settled — examine well. Therefore there is no difficulty: there is a dispute in the Gemara if fire is because of its substance or because of monetary value; we hold because of substance; the Navi in Bava Kamma chapter 2 questioned: if fire is because of substance, it should be forbidden to kindle a lamp on Shabbat even if kindled on erev Shabbat; they answered it is as if he did everything at permitted time on erev Shabbat; if so, at least his acts exist and all is considered his act, and again it is human act and extinguishing is not required — it is no worse than accidental kindling. Therefore the Gemara that challenges from extinguishing and raising — it is that otherwise one could not challenge the view requiring extinguishing — one could say R' Yehuda bar Nachmani holds like the view fire is because of monetary value, and then there is no human act and it is as kindled by itself, worse than accidental kindling; therefore it challenges him: even so raising should be required; but for us who hold fire is because of substance, all kindling is as his act, and therefore not worse than accidental kindling; therefore the Rambam wrote only because kindling accomplishes the mitzvah therefore one extinguishes — it fits well — examine well. (Same seif) If he kindled inside and took it outside he has not fulfilled, etc. NB: See in my works on Orach Chayim year 5566 what I wrote resolving the Tur's words; see Bach and Taz who wondered why this reason is needed since we hold kindling accomplishes the mitzvah; see in my works Orach Chayim year 5549 siman 673 to resolve this. It also appears there is a practical difference if a courtyard has two entrances — must kindle at both; Ran wrote since it is only because of suspicion, blessing is not required; in my humble opinion that does not appear correct, for the baraita taught: if he kindled inside and took outside he did nothing; from "he did nothing" it is proven blessing is required; the Gemara concludes the reason from the viewer saying for his need — how did he do nothing? It is proven that because of suspicion blessing is required; therefore it fits that Tur and Shulchan Aruch cited this reason to prove: if for suspicion blessing is required, from "he did nothing" likewise with two entrances blessing is required even though only suspicion. However one may distinguish: this suspicion "for his need" means he kindled for need — then he did not publicize the miracle at all, therefore must bless; but with two entrances, although they suspect he did not kindle Hanukkah, nevertheless he truly publicized the miracle — therefore one could say no blessing is required — such one could say; however the Tur may hold they are equal — examine. I was uncertain: if everyone used only wax lights and their custom was not olive oil, and now one kindled olive oil, or he was mehader and held many lights in hand for the days — do we say the viewer saying for his need does not apply, for such a lamp is not normally for need, and it is not normal to use many lights — he will be compelled to say it is for Hanukkah; or even then do we decree the Rabbis did not distinguish in their enactment? — requires study for law — examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (Same, seif 3) And there are those who say a minor who reached chinuch may discharge, etc. NB: See Magen Avraham below siman 689 and in laws of Megillah — he questioned Shulchan Aruch's contradictory words: there he ruled plainly a minor never discharges in any way and did not bring the Orach Mishpat; here he brought the Orach Mishpat who holds a minor who reached chinuch discharges the adult. He wrote it is strained to distinguish between Hanukkah light and Megillah — in Ran it implies they are equal — see there. In my humble opinion it resolves correctly: regarding the reason one discharges another — there is a dispute if it is because of partnership or agency; in our novellae on Megillah siman 689 chapter 4 we questioned Tosafot's contradictory words: in Berachot they wrote in the evening prayer a minor does not discharge an adult because two rabbinic matters cannot discharge one rabbinic matter; we wrote: granted for partnership it fits, since they are not similar and their obligations are not equal, one cannot discharge the other; but for agency — if so it is as if he himself blesses — why does not two rabbinic discharge one rabbinic? Tosafot in Gittin hold agency applies to a minor in a matter that suits him; if so, since the minor is obligated in Birkat HaMazon, it suits him and he is considered the adult's agent — why is the minor not his agent? — see what is written there. However now it appears well according to Maharit in responsa who holds agency does not work for an oath because words are not entrusted to an agent — see there. True, elsewhere I wondered on him — one could say "words are not entrusted to an agent" means another becomes agent, but one can be agent even for words; nevertheless Maharit holds words are not entrusted to an agent and there is no agency; therefore Berachot fits: Birkat HaMazon is only words, agency does not apply, only partnership — therefore two rabbinic do not discharge one rabbinic; but where there is act, one can be agent — two rabbinic can discharge one rabbinic by agency. Therefore Hanukkah fits, for it is act and agency applies; but Megillah is words, agency does not apply — therefore two rabbinic do not discharge one rabbinic. Therefore Ran and such hold an agent can nullify another's chametz; but Ran brought other views nullification by agent does not help — they dispute Maharit's view if agency applies to words. Therefore Ran for his view that agency applies to words — truly Megillah equals Hanukkah; but for us legally, in Pesach laws he ruled like those who hold an agent can nullify; nevertheless in Megillah he ruled properly no minor discharges, lest we change — perhaps like those who hold even in Hanukkah, being act, two rabbinic do not discharge one rabbinic; and if you say like Orach Mishpat who holds like Hanukkah a minor discharges — the main reason is agency; if so, perhaps the law follows those who hold words cannot have an agent, and Megillah is only partnership, and certainly two rabbinic do not discharge one rabbinic. Therefore since there is room to be stringent, he did not heed the Orach Mishpat at all; but in Hanukkah, being act and agency applies, he brought the Orach Mishpat properly — one can say since it is by agency, two rabbinic can discharge one rabbinic; the reasoning fits as I wrote — correct in this — examine well.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] The viewer, etc. Bach questioned: in Shabbat 22a the reason is kindling must be in its place, and Rambam wrote so; he answered the Gemara teaches even for us who kindle inside, if he took them outside he has not fulfilled — the viewer, etc.; he questioned on this: in any case he should also write the reason kindling must be in its place, which is also halacha. It appears to me he follows his reason written earlier that there is a practical difference: for the reason kindling in its place — also on Shabbat and Yom Tov it is required; but for the viewer reason — not required for Shabbat and Yom Tov lights, for there is no pirsumei nisa — it fits; I wonder, for Mahariv in Pesach laws wrote the viewer reason is also required on Shabbat and Yom Tov. I saw in responsa Beit Yaakov siman 53 who wrote the practical difference mentioned in the name of Mordechai; he did not examine — Mordechai in chapter BeMa Madlikin did not write it at all, only a law of Shabbat and Yom Tov on the reason kindling in its place, because we hold kindling accomplishes the mitzvah, therefore the viewer difficulty is not needed — as our question. Truly the viewer reason is as Mahariv wrote. Now it fits in Tosafot d.h. de'iba'i, etc., why they did not write this practical difference; with this the Bach's first answer is also rejected — the Taz in his length followed the Tur that in conclusion the kindling-in-place reason is rejected even for the view kindling accomplishes the mitzvah, since there is no practical difference — why say the mitzvah is rejected; and further it is difficult for him, for there is practical difference — if so, why did Rama and Levush rule in siman 663 seif 10 that also on Shabbat and Yom Tov it must be in its place; and in any case Beit Yaakov's responsum is strained with many strains. It is also difficult on what he explained Rashi's view: perhaps for the view placement accomplishes the mitzvah he agrees kindling is also mitzvah, only placement is primary; for the view kindling accomplishes the mitzvah there is no mitzvah in placement at all; therefore the Gemara says for the view kindling, etc., therefore he did nothing — if so, why does the Gemara challenge Rava who said he held Hanukkah lights and did nothing — learn placement accomplishes the mitzvah; still kindling is also mitzvah — what does "he did nothing" mean? Also what he answers Tosafot's difficulty d.h. mechabeh, etc., on 23a — therefore it says kindling since it is also mitzvah — he did not examine, for Tosafot concluded: is a deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor worse than one who kindled? He means: even for deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor the viewer is not required to kindle — this is the practical difference as Tosafot wrote earlier. It should also be difficult why he explained afterward that the Tur rules for the view kindling accomplishes the mitzvah placement is also mitzvah — if so, what does the Gemara say except if kindling accomplishes the mitzvah it fits — still "he must place it" is difficult since placement is also mitzvah, and he himself explained so afterward — he contradicts himself.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ג: Magen Avraham was not placed in this answer, for Rama wrote above in siman 663 that Shabbat lights also require kindling in their place; therefore he grasped Bach's main first answer. Regarding Bach's question that he should in any case also write the reason kindling in its place is required — perhaps Magen Avraham holds: here regarding Hanukkah light there is no practical difference, therefore Beit Yosef did not give the kindling-in-place reason; or Beit Yosef agrees with Magen Avraham to Bach's answer that for conclusion he does not require kindling in its place — he did not cite Magen Avraham's first answer, only for us according to what Rama wrote in siman 663 that Shabbat lights also require kindling in their place; and Rama must not have emended here also the kindling-in-place reason because he relied on siman 663.
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (7) And he holds it in his hand, etc. — the Taz's view is specifically while he holds it the entire time of his mitzvah; but if he holds it in his hand a short time and afterward places it while burning, he has fulfilled; however several recent authorities are uncertain about this, and their view is one should not kindle until they are first placed in their location.
peri-megadim/3:א: And so Taz Shabbat 22b d.h. hayah tafus and d.h. v'amad — not precise; there is some doubt, for "stood" implies some time — what is "stood"? Until it went out? — he kindled in his hand and placed it afterward and fulfilled; for the questioner, placement accomplishes the mitzvah — certainly placing afterward fulfills; for Acharonim the essence of the mitzvah is specifically thus, as written in letter 2; for Rashi one could say not at all — he did not fulfill at all if he placed them only a short time even though he did not remain half an hour — b'dieved at least he fulfilled; for conclusion the viewer, etc., is specifically held and stood the entire time — if not fulfilled; the viewer, etc. — see letter 2: if he placed a short time, b'dieved at least he fulfilled; l'chatchila one could say even kindling must be after placement — Eliyah Rabbah. Peri Chadash: known Hanukkah lamps with eight outlets — the viewer, etc.; nevertheless l'chatchila he should appear to place and afterward kindle; b'dieved by holding in his hand the entire time he fulfilled. What the Mechaber wrote in seif 2 — he put oil afterward as measure — does not help; Peri Chadash wrote he returns and blesses — requires study, for there are two answers in the Gemara, and perhaps for the measure and first answer one need not put oil as measure — how bless a doubtful blessing? See siman 672 — requires study.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: {Rama: Seif 3} And there are those who say regarding a minor who reached chinuch. See below siman 689 seif 2 and Magen Avraham there s.k. 4.
turei-zahav/1:ב: That the viewer says for his need. In the Gemara we challenge the view that kindling accomplishes the mitzvah from Rava: he held Hanukkah lights and did nothing — learn placement accomplishes the mitzvah; we answer there: the viewer says for his need — he relies on a baraita Rava said: he kindled inside and took out — he did nothing; unless kindling accomplishes the mitzvah in its place is required, for since this is its mitzvah it must be done in the place of obligation; if placement accomplishes the mitzvah, why did he do nothing? We answer there too: the viewer says for his need — he kindled; if so, it implies for the view kindling accomplishes the mitzvah the viewer reason is not needed, only because kindling must be in its place, as the questioner holds. Why did Tur and Shulchan Aruch write the viewer reason? It appears the Tur deduced Hagahot Maimoniyot's wording there: it also implies it is not so reasonable here as in Rava's first case — therefore the questioner: specifically in Rava's first case held in hand it is reasonable the viewer says for his need, for such is people's way to hold in hand when using anything; but kindling inside it is not so reasonable to say thus — therefore he labored to find for the view kindling accomplishes the mitzvah an answer: because the mitzvah must be outside where the Hanukkah light belongs by Talmud law; but for the view placement accomplishes the mitzvah it is difficult — we answer here too there is nevertheless room to err to the viewer, since he does not do the kindling in the place of obligation which is outside, and it is unnecessary labor, but certainly he has some need inside where he kindles; since so, even for the view kindling l'shem mitzvah the kindling-in-place reason is not needed — we also say this reason because of the viewer, for otherwise one must say he holds the viewer reason from Rava's first case holding Hanukkah lights — therefore our Rabbi mentioned only this viewer reason in both — this is obvious in my humble opinion.
